svg.text: IF YOU'RE SO SMART, WHY ARE YOU NOT · PRODUCTIVE / PRODUCTIVITY ENHANCEMENT · PART 7.1
FOUR HARNESSES. EACH ADDS ONE ORGAN OF AUTONOMY. PICK THE SMALLEST THAT FITS.
four configs of one worker · read left → right as the cords fall away
operator's reach — taps fewer cords each bay →

g.text: you are the loop, the memory
save the context once · this blog runs here.
starts every run already knowing who you are.

svg.text: + ITS OWN TRIGGER · a clock or an event

g.text: it wakes itself — the work happens whether or
not you're thinking about it. AI I use → AI that runs.

svg.text: + ITS OWN COMPUTER · a dedicated machine

g.text: its own VPS / machine · persistent · always on.
an assistant you open → a worker that's simply

svg.text: TASK-MATCH SELECTOR ▸ route each job UP to the smallest sufficient rung — don't reach past it

g.text: A PROVEN PROCESS THAT SHOULD NEVER SLEEP
give it a machine — only after L3 proves it

svg.text: the model is identical in every bay — only the harness around it grows
MODEL CAPABILITY — FLAT · same model in every bay
SETUP COST / INFRASTRUCTURE grows fat left → right — more to stand up, more to run
PICK THE SMALLEST HARNESS THE TASK PULLS FOR.

g.text: L1 CHAT · L2 PROJECTS · L3 SCHEDULED · L4 FULL RUNTIME
← 3.1 instructions = the L2 memory · 4.0 / 4.1 knowledge it reaches · 6.0 match-the-rung discipline
→ 7.2 persistent memory = state that survives across runs

svg.text: the agent doesn't get smarter up the bench — it gets more self-sufficient, and more expensive to stand up.
ALWAYS-ON OVER AN UNPROVEN PROCESS = PROBLEMS, NON-STOP.
prove it at L3 first — then give it a machine.
